newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel provident funds not dumping stocks - report.
newsitem.headline: Israel provident funds not dumping stocks - report.

text.p: Israeli provident funds have not dumped shares in recent months to meet the massive public redemptions of the past months, Meitav Investment and Securities said in a report.

Redemptions from provident funds reached 2.7 billion shekels in the second quarter of the year, the report said. But Meitav estimates the funds still hold 11.1 percent (or 12.2 billion shekels) of the total value of shares in the market (about 109.7 billion shekels), unchanged from March.

Meitav said it expects public redemptions from provident funds to rise to 6.5 billion shekels in the third quarter. "It will be interesting to see the behaviour of provident fund managers in the stock market in the coming quarter," the report said.

Stocks accounted for 12 percent of the total assets of the five major provident fund managers surveyed by Meitav. This level is unchanged from March but lower than in December 1995, when stocks accounted for 12.9 percent of their assets.
Their assets totalled 73 billion shekels in June, representing 65 percent of the total assets of Israeli provident funds.

Provident funds are long-term savings funds with special tax benefits. A weak stock and bond market has hurt their performance, triggering off a wave of public redemptions that was aggravated by media reports concerning the rising level of redemptions.
